$comment: The human-readable tables in the spec and this file must agree; the linter enforces it.
No tool, script, agent or CI job writes here (SPEC-GOV-001): changes are reviewed commits.

entries.title: No tool, script, agent or CI job may write to spec/. A
entries.normativeText: No tool, script, agent or CI job may write to `spec/`. A conformance divergence is reported as a finding and never resolved by editing the spec.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: Every SPEC-ID carries exactly one of PROPOSED, ACTIVE, RETIRED
entries.normativeText: Every SPEC-ID carries exactly one of PROPOSED, ACTIVE, RETIRED. CI enforces conformance for ACTIVE ids only.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: A PROPOSED id becomes ACTIVE only in a commit whose tree
entries.normativeText: A PROPOSED id becomes ACTIVE only in a commit whose tree already satisfies its conformance predicates; the linter refuses an activation whose predicates do not hold in that same tree.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: An ACTIVE id's normative text is immutable: the linter compares
entries.normativeText: An ACTIVE id's normative text is immutable: the linter compares it to the text at its activation commit in the integration branch's history and fails on any difference.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: An ACTIVE id is retired only by an activation commit that names
entries.normativeText: An ACTIVE id is retired only by an activation commit that names its successor, and the successor names it back. A SPEC-ID is never reused and never deleted.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: Every ACTIVE id names at least one code anchor, at least one
entries.normativeText: Every ACTIVE id names at least one code anchor, at least one test that fails when the invariant breaks, and every `[SPEC-…]` annotation in the tree resolves to a registered id.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: One SPEC-ID binds exactly one refusable behavior: if two
entries.normativeText: One SPEC-ID binds exactly one refusable behavior: if two distinct mutations require two different sentences to explain the break, they are two ids.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: Every digest this system publishes is computed over the
entries.normativeText: Every digest this system publishes is computed over the canonical framed serialization of §6b, never over a concatenation.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: Mutation evidence is a closed record of commit, patch digest
entries.normativeText: Mutation evidence is a closed record of commit, patch digest, command and expected failure; an activation without it is refused.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: The audit stages run in order — traceability linter
entries.normativeText: The audit stages run in order — traceability linter, conformance checks, semantic interpretation, independent review, human decision — and no stage substitutes another.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: The auditor persona approves nothing, accepts no risk, performs
entries.normativeText: The auditor persona approves nothing, accepts no risk, performs no effect, edits nothing, and holds no protocol seat before a reviewed protocol amendment.

entries.title: Every audit report names its audited commit, its reviewed base
entries.normativeText: Every audit report names its audited commit, its reviewed base, and the digests of the diff, the spec set, the mechanical reports, the input bundle and the persona.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: Every audit run pins its model, profile, timeout, token ceiling
entries.normativeText: Every audit run pins its model, profile, timeout, token ceiling and cost ceiling; a run that hits a ceiling reports INCOMPLETE, which is never read as PASS.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: Each paid audit run happens under its own spend authorization
entries.normativeText: Each paid audit run happens under its own spend authorization, issued by Zamp and covering that run only.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: A runbook confers no authority: it documents how an operation
entries.normativeText: A runbook confers no authority: it documents how an operation is performed and never whether it may be.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: A document that mutates cloud state declares cloudMutation
entries.normativeText: A document that mutates cloud state declares `cloudMutation: true` and depends on a cloud authorization; preparing a CloudFormation change set is cloud mutation.

entries.title: Runbook frontmatter carries exactly the closed key set

entries.title: A kind: runbook document covers exactly one operation with one
entries.normativeText: A `kind: runbook` document covers exactly one operation with one decision; a `kind: index` document links runbooks and holds no commands.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: Every command in a runbook names the actor that performs it
entries.normativeText: Every command in a runbook names the actor that performs it, and that actor is permitted to perform it by `spec/authority-policy.json`.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — enforcement tooling does not exist yet (§7a)

entries.title: A cloud authorization is authored only after a read-only
entries.normativeText: A cloud authorization is authored only after a read-only binding operation has produced the exact manifest and assembly digest it must name.

entries.title: The evidence of a cloud effect is a complete artifact bound to
entries.normativeText: The evidence of a cloud effect is a complete artifact bound to run id, decisionId, release SHA, stack group and plan digest; a truncated excerpt is not evidence.
entries.mutationEvidence: code + tests reviewed in I3/I3-3: closed record, correlation proven before anything runs, honest partial on every halt, no account-bearing ARN; the record is bounded in UTF-8 BYTES to the NARROWEST hop — 100k bytes, with margin under the single Linux envp entry (MAX_ARG_STRLEN 128 KiB) that injects it into the materializer; every wider hop (the ~1MB job-output store) is satisfied a fortiori — and a plan whose record cannot cross REFUSES (PLAN_RENDERING_TOO_LARGE): evidence is reshaped by named code, never truncated, transport loss is a red run, and the materializer is proven by EXECUTION at near-cap size, byte for byte

entries.title: Change sets prepared for a plan that will not execute are
entries.normativeText: Change sets prepared for a plan that will not execute are deleted under their own authorization; they are never left to expire.

entries.title: The deploy child receives exactly the stack ids the manifest

entries.mutationEvidence: code + tests reviewed, reversion proven

entries.normativeText: The cloud authorization value satisfies a closed ten-key schema with `issue` pinned to 70, `mode` in {plan_only, deploy} and a `decisionId` matching its documented shape; any other shape refuses.

entries.title: The plan is a set of named CloudFormation change sets
entries.normativeText: The plan is a set of named CloudFormation change sets: `plan_only` prepares them and `deploy` executes exactly those, addressed by their immutable change-set ids.

entries.title: A deploy executes only a stack group the reviewed plan-group

entries.title: Every DescribeChangeSet response is validated against the

entries.title: In the plan rendering, no value observed in a change set is

entries.title: Child stdout and stderr are never reproduced; a failure records
entries.normativeText: Child stdout and stderr are never reproduced; a failure records the exit code, per-stream byte counts and one digest over the framed streams. This digest is the named exception to SPEC-DEPLOY-006: it covers whole streams that are never published, not a value in the rendering, so it offers no per-value oracle.

entries.title: The target account is resolved again immediately before the

entries.title: An authorization instant is accepted only as strict RFC3339 UTC
entries.normativeText: An authorization instant is accepted only as strict RFC3339 UTC that round-trips through the calendar; a normalized or offset instant refuses.

entries.normativeText: An authorization is valid only while `approvedAt` ≤ now < `expiresAt`, with `expiresAt − approvedAt` at most one hour.

entries.title: The authorization window is re-checked as the last operation
entries.normativeText: The authorization window is re-checked as the last operation before EACH change-set execution; a window that lapses mid-sequence stops the remaining executions.

entries.title: The cloud authorization value has EXACTLY these ten keys —
entries.normativeText: The cloud authorization value has EXACTLY these ten keys — `issue`, `mode`, `decisionId`, `releaseSha`, `environment`, `manifestDigest`, `stacks`, `planDigest`, `approvedAt`, `expiresAt` — no key absent and none unknown, with the per-key and per-mode constraints of §8a. Any other shape, and any effect outside the value's `mode`, refuses.

entries.title: The cloud authorization schema carries an abandon mode, and an
entries.normativeText: The cloud authorization schema carries an `abandon` mode, and an abandon run executes no change set and prepares none.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — absorbed into SPEC-DEPLOY-019 before activation (§4)

entries.title: The stack-record cleanup decision is a closed nine-key value
entries.normativeText: The stack-record cleanup decision is a closed nine-key value (§8b): each key holds its exact grammar, `stackId` is a positionally validated CloudFormation stack ARN whose embedded region, account and name EQUAL the record's `region`, `account` and `stackName`, and the decision is valid only while `observedAt <= now < observedAt + 15 minutes`, a future instant refusing. The performer re-observes the same identity, status and window immediately before deleting. The activation commit must contain the instance parser and its adversarial tests, and that parser must re-check — immediately before the effect — that the acceptance is unexpired at that moment, that the §6b bundle digest it recomputes over the presented cleanup value equals `coversCleanupAuthorizationSha256`, and that the value's `decisionId` equals `coversCleanupDecisionId`. The residual TOCTOU that no re-observation can close leaves the effect without an executable procedure until Zamp records acceptance as the closed `riskAcceptance` record — a boolean is not a decision, and a free-text record is not an enforceable one.
entries.mutationEvidence: policy data + tests reviewed in this commit; instance parser awaits activation; no procedure exists

entries.title: Deleting the empty stack record a CREATE change set leaves
entries.normativeText: Deleting the empty stack record a CREATE change set leaves behind is an effect distinct from deleting a change set, authorized by its own out-of-band instrument (§8b) that no lane can read, and no automated lane performs it: `DeleteStack` accepts no expected-status precondition, so an observed `REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS` cannot constrain the delete that follows it, and the release concurrency lock binds only this repository's lanes. A lane that would delete a stack record refuses; the condition is reported and resolved by a separate human decision.
entries.mutationEvidence: policy data + test reviewed in this commit; no lane may perform it

entries.title: A bind_only dispatch terminates after the preflight and is
entries.normativeText: A `bind_only` dispatch terminates after the preflight and is structurally unable to enter a stage that prepares or executes change sets, whatever the Environment holds at any moment of the run.
entries.mutationEvidence: code + tests reviewed in I2: mode-gated on the immutable dispatch input, no id-token, no OIDC consumer, DAG-terminal

entries.title: Every dispatch carries a caller-generated correlation id
entries.normativeText: Every dispatch carries a caller-generated correlation id matching exactly `^cba-70-[0-9a-f]{32}$`; a dispatch whose id does not match is refused in the preflight, before any credentialed stage. The run's NAME is exactly `cba-release <mode> <correlationId>` and nothing else, so a run is selected by EQUALITY on its complete name — never by substring — and is identifiable from run metadata alone, before any artifact exists. The same id appears inside the structured uploaded artifact, together with the release SHA the run acted on, which is what a reviewer compares against the request; a run's `headSha` is the dispatch ref's tip and is never that comparison.
entries.mutationEvidence: code + tests reviewed in I2: closed-grammar refusal executed against the real script; run name and binding artifact pinned

entries.title: Run resolution is bounded and unambiguous: the workflow is
entries.normativeText: Run resolution is bounded and unambiguous: the workflow is pinned by FILE identity inside the helper (`release-pilot.yml` — a display name is not an identity, and no caller may supply another); the query pins `--branch main` and `--event workflow_dispatch`, matches the complete run name by EQUALITY, and is EXHAUSTIVE OR STOPS — a page that returns as many rows as requested refuses as truncated rather than proving uniqueness from the newest slice. It polls at most ten times with thirty seconds between attempts and no wait after the last, stops on zero matches after the bound or more than one at ANY query, and every external call carries a reviewed wall-clock deadline with a named timeout stop — ten attempts do not bound a stalled call or an endlessly queued run. After the run reaches a terminal conclusion, the SAME query must re-observe exactly the same single run id immediately before the artifact is accepted.
entries.mutationEvidence: helper + simulated-`gh` tests reviewed in this commit; the run name itself awaits the workflow

entries.title: Evidence is accepted only from a run that reached a terminal
entries.normativeText: Evidence is accepted only from a run that reached a terminal conclusion, identified by the correlation id it published in run metadata, whose artifact repeats that correlation id and names the release SHA the request dispatched, and whose provenance (run id, conclusion) is verified. The run's `headSha` is never used to identify the release.
entries.mutationEvidence: none — awaiting SPEC-LANE-006

entries.title: When a sequence halts, the output names exactly which change
entries.normativeText: When a sequence halts, the output names exactly which change sets executed and states that the remaining ones did not.

entries.title: In every credentialed job, synthesis completes before the
entries.normativeText: In every credentialed job, synthesis completes before the pinned OIDC consumer step, and after that step ONLY the reviewed entrypoints and the evidence-output reader execute — no action step and no package-manager command, ever, because `id-token: write` is job-scoped and no scrub can remove the ability to mint a fresh token. Evidence leaves the lane exclusively from a job that never holds `id-token`.
